chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān and Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh and al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no Jumuʿah in travel, nor Fiṭr, nor Aḍḥā.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state of being a traveler subject to legal concessions

ai.seo_question: Are Jumuʿah and the ʿĪd prayers obligatory for a traveler in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that Jumuʿah prayer and the salat of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr and ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā do not apply to the traveler. It is cited in the context of the falling away of the two ʿĪd prayers from the musāfir and reflects travel-related concessions in worship.
